tab.reason: Container and item are inverted, not merely the wrong element: daisyTab emits <button class="tabs"> and daisyTabTab emits <div class="tab">. Fixing it means swapping the component/part classification, which renames every function in the file.

calendar.reason: DaisyUI documents Cally's custom element <calendar-date>, and kotlinx.html has no tag class for a custom element. Needs a decision — a generic custom-tag escape hatch, or skipping the component — rather than an element swap.

badge/badge-neutral.reason: daisyBadge renders <span> deliberately: every one of DaisyUI's seven <span> examples sits inside a heading or a paragraph, where a <div> is invalid HTML, so <span> is the only element valid in all 54 documented positions. This class is documented on <div> alone, and one generated function renders one element — kotlinx.html cannot pick by context, since H1 and P are themselves FlowContent. Permanent; see the issue.

dock/dock-active.reason: Declared on the container's function (<div>) while DaisyUI puts it on a child <button> the library generates no function for, so a caller cannot reach it. NOT the join-item shape: measured 2026-09-19 at v5.7.17, all 7 sightings sit on a bare <button> with no daisyUI class beside it, where join-item's 72 sightings all carry a component class. A scope member needs a function to overload and there is none.

dropdown/dropdown-close.reason: daisyDropdown renders <details> deliberately: the <div> shape is the popover variant, which needs attributes the generator cannot emit and produced a dropdown that could not open. This class is documented on the <div> shape alone. The CSS attaches to .dropdown whatever the tag, so this is a documentation divergence, not a rendering one. Permanent until a daisyDropdownPopover exists; see the issue.
